policy_decision.rationale: Multi-candidate routing achieves meaningful physical SWAP and depth reductions on dense, non-adjacent entangling circuits (e.g. QFT and logical swap stress), but incurs a linear compile-time growth factor (~8.7x at B=16) with saturating returns for B >= 8. On already-adjacent or linear topologies, search yields zero SWAP reduction while still consuming 4x-16x compilation time. Therefore, deterministic single-candidate routing (Budget=1) must remain the default, keeping multi-candidate routing strictly opt-in.
